label: Whatever has esse in re is CONCRETE_6 in the profile
paraphrase: OPEN interpretation premise, analyst formulation: one direction of the CONCRETE_6 calibration of the profile's free concreteness predicate. Whatever has esse in re (HasEsseInRe InAct esse, InAct x esse: being in the first way of De ente c.1, DEF-CONCRETE-ESSE-IN-RE) satisfies m.concrete. HasEsseInRe reads the shared InAct inclusively (formally or eminently, DISAMB-IN-ACT), here and wherever this batch uses it. It is the left-to-right half of the concreteIsEsse field of CausalPowerConcreteness.EsseIntendedProfile (owner-adopted sense of concrete, #1103), stated for the Profile and InAct of the stage-two composition, where the statements on m.concrete already link CONCRETE_6. The converse (concrete things have esse in re) is not stated or used. With the existence-to-act contract STMT-EXISTING-IN-ACT-AT it commits the profile to reading existence at w as existence in re: nothing non-concrete exists at w. A theorist who counts a Form, set or law as existing at w without esse in re rejects that contract or this calibration, not a causal premise. Under the causal-criterion sense CONCRETE_5 the stage-two concreteness clauses would mean something else; this premise fixes CONCRETE_6. No independent warrant is recorded for it beyond the owner-adopted sense.
